# Olivier Toubia

> Olivier Toubia is the Glaubinger Professor of Business and Senior Vice Dean for Curriculum and Instruction at Columbia Business School. He is a marketing scholar who works on innovation, idea generation, creativity, preference measurement, computational social science, and generative AI. Recent work covers digital twins and synthetic data built with large language models.

This file is a plain-text summary of https://otoubia.github.io/homepage/ for language models and AI assistants. The homepage and his CV are the authoritative sources (CV last updated October 2026).

- [Homepage](https://otoubia.github.io/homepage/): full CV-based profile

## Current roles

- Glaubinger Professor of Business, Columbia Business School (2012–present)
- Senior Vice Dean for Curriculum and Instruction, Columbia Business School (2026–present)
- Associate Editor, Journal of Consumer Research (2026–present)
- Associate Editor, Journal of Marketing (2025–present)
- Member of the Advisory Board, Marketing Science (2025–present)

## Past roles (selected)

- Editor-in-Chief, Marketing Science (2022–2024)
- Chair of the Marketing Division, Columbia Business School (2019–2022)
- Faculty Director, The Eugene Lang Center for Entrepreneurship, Columbia Business School (2016–2019)
- VP Education, INFORMS Society for Marketing Science (2016–2018)
- At Columbia Business School since 2004: Assistant Professor (2004–2007), David W. Zalaznick Associate Professor (2007–2010), Associate Professor with tenure (2010–2011), Professor of Marketing (2011–2012)

## Education

- Ph.D. in Marketing, MIT Sloan School of Management (2004)
- S.M. in Operations Research, Massachusetts Institute of Technology (2001)
- Ingénieur, Ecole Centrale Paris (2000)

## Research interests

Innovation; idea generation; creativity; preference measurement (conjoint analysis); computational social science; generative AI.

## Major honors

- John Little Award (best marketing paper in Marketing Science or Management Science): 2003, 2006, 2017, 2018
- Don Morrison Long Term Impact Award: 2022
- INFORMS Society for Marketing Science Long Term Impact Award: 2016
- Paul E. Green Award (Journal of Marketing Research): 2015
- Don Lehmann Award: 2012
- Frank M. Bass Outstanding Dissertation Award and John A. Howard AMA Dissertation Award: 2005

## Selected recent publications

- Peng, Brucks, Gui, Merlau, et al., and Toubia (2026). "Digital Twins are Funhouse Mirrors: Five Systematic Distortions." Science Advances, 12(36): eaeh8260.
- Toubia, Gui, Peng, Merlau, Li, and Chen (2025). "Database Report: Twin-2K-500: A Dataset for Building Digital Twins of over 2,000 People Based on Their Answers to over 500 Questions." Marketing Science, 44(6), 1446–1455.
- Toubia (2026). "Synthetic Data and Digital Twins: The Hype, The Facts, the Promise." Current Opinion in Psychology, forthcoming.
- Toubia and Berger (2026). "Optimally Sequencing Semantic Search Predicts Creativity." PLOS ONE, 21(6): e0352328.
- Luo and Toubia (2026). "Discrimination Against Femininity in Headshots: A Field Experiment with AI-Enabled Controllable Stimuli Generation." Marketing Science (Frontiers), forthcoming.
- Liu and Toubia (2026). "The Effects of Search Interface on Consumer Preferences: Evidence from a Randomized Experiment." Marketing Science, forthcoming.
- Shaddy, Friedman, and Toubia (2026). "Fairness Perceptions in Demographic Targeting." Journal of Consumer Research, 53(1), 22–47.
- Brucks and Toubia (2025). "Prompt Architecture Induces Methodological Artifacts in Large Language Models." PLOS ONE, 20(4).
- Dahl, Noble, Schreier, and Toubia (2025). "Better Innovation for a Better World." Journal of Marketing, 89(6), 100–118.
- Berger and Toubia (2024). "The Topography of Thought." PNAS Nexus, 3(5), pgae163.
- Toubia, Berger, and Eliashberg (2021). "How Quantifying the Shape of Stories Predicts Their Success." Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 118(26).

- Toubia (2006). "Idea Generation, Creativity, and Incentives." Marketing Science, 25(5). John Little Award; ISMS Long Term Impact Award.
- Stephen and Toubia (2010). "Deriving Value from Social Commerce Networks." Journal of Marketing Research, 47(2). Don Lehmann Award.
- Toubia and Stephen (2013). "Intrinsic versus Image-Related Utility in Social Media: Why Do People Contribute Content to Twitter?" Marketing Science, 32(3). Don Morrison Long Term Impact Award.
- Yang, Toubia, and de Jong (2015). "A Bounded Rationality Model of Information Search and Choice in Preference Measurement." Journal of Marketing Research, 52(2). Paul E. Green Award.

- Liu and Toubia (2018). "A Semantic Approach for Estimating Consumer Content Preferences from Online Search Queries." Marketing Science, 37(6). John Little Award.
